# UUIDv7 primary keys generated by PostgreSQL for domain tables; bigint for append-only logs

Every table that appears in a URL or an API response (users, nurse profiles, units, rosters and
their versions, solves, requests, swaps) uses a UUIDv7 primary key generated by PostgreSQL 18's
native `uuidv7()` as the column default (Django 6.1 exposes it as a database default). The keys
are time-ordered, so they index and sort like serial numbers, and they are not guessable or
enumerable, so a nurse cannot walk other units' rosters by incrementing an id. Append-only
internal tables (audit log entries, solve progress rows, queue tables) keep bigint identity
keys, where volume matters and nothing is exposed.

UUIDv4 was rejected (random keys fragment B-tree indexes); application-generated UUIDv7 was
rejected in favour of the database default so that rows inserted by migrations, scripts or the
admin get the same kind of key.
